deficits.evidence: No continuous sidewalk; people and parked cars share the edge of the road.
deficits.suggestion: Construct a 1.5 m paved footway on the left, set back from the parked cars.

deficits.evidence: The right edge is an uneven dirt strip with no defined path.
deficits.suggestion: Lay a 1.5 m concrete footway along the right side in front of the unfinished building.

deficits.evidence: A row of parked vehicles occupies the only usable strip on the left.
deficits.suggestion: Mark a no-parking zone on the left to keep the footway clear.

deficits.evidence: A parked pickup and construction materials block the right edge.
deficits.suggestion: Provide a designated parking bay away from the right footway.

deficits.evidence: Broken paving and debris are scattered along the left edge.
deficits.suggestion: Resurface the left footway to remove the broken sections.

deficits.evidence: Loose rubble and uneven ground are visible on the right.
deficits.suggestion: Clear the rubble and level the right footway.

deficits.evidence: People are seen crossing at an unmarked point with no facility.
deficits.suggestion: Install a marked pedestrian crossing at the junction with dropped kerbs.

deficits.evidence: No dropped kerbs are visible at the crossing point.
deficits.suggestion: Add dropped kerbs at both ends of the new crossing.

ratings.reason: The left edge is a dirt strip with parked cars, confirming the lack of a footway, but the available space for construction is unclear.
The right side is an uneven dirt area in front of the unfinished building, confirming the deficit, though space for a new footway is not fully clear.
Parked vehicles are clearly visible on the left, and marking a no-parking zone is a realistic and specific measure.
A pickup truck and rubble are visible on the right, and providing a designated parking bay is a feasible solution.
Broken paving and debris are visible on the left, and resurfacing is a standard and feasible repair.
Loose rubble and uneven ground are clearly visible on the right, and clearing/levelling is a feasible action.
People are seen crossing at an unmarked point, and installing a marked crossing is a standard and feasible improvement.
The absence of dropped kerbs at the crossing point is evident, and adding them is a standard and feasible measure.
